acceptance: bundle-fetch proceeds as soon as the producing run's bundle-building job has succeeded and the bundle artifact is listed, regardless of other jobs in that run; it still fails closed when that job failed or the artifact is missing
If the bundle job itself is still queued or running, the existing bounded wait applies to that job
Tests cover a run whose bundle job succeeded while a later job is queued, a failed bundle job, and a missing artifact
The first core-bundle dispatch deploy after merge whose producing run still has a queued trailing job deploys without waiting for it; run id recorded
context:
Found 2026-10-31 while checking the first deploys after the bounded-resolver and bundle-order changes; the wait predates them.

Closed 2026-11-01 under the owner's decision to close on first post-merge evidence. Live: production deploy 41268048597 at bce1677 succeeded (fetched site-inputs-2ab29ce3 from run 41267301518). No core-bundle dispatch with a queued trailing job has run since merge, so criterion 4's exact case has no live run yet.
description: scripts/bundle-fetch.mjs (wait added in #47, 2026-10-19) waits up to 600 s for the producing core site-inputs run to complete before downloading its bundle. Core dispatches the bundle as soon as its 'build bundle' job succeeds, but the run then still has a trailing job ('close the bundle-failure issue') that needs a runner. Under the org's shared 20-job cap that job can wait far longer than 600 s, so the deploy fails even though the bundle artifact is ready: deploy run 41250152375 (2026-10-31, core d1a724dec) waited on producing run 41248555826, whose 'build bundle' job finished at 22:53:14Z while 'close the bundle-failure issue' only started at 23:22:06Z; the deploy gave up at 23:13:57Z ('did not complete within the 600s wait cap'), posted to #58 and the core relay.
